summary: A parameterized constructor lets you give an object its starting values in the same line that creates it. A class can keep its default constructor too, and Java picks the one whose parameters match your arguments.
notes: Both constructors are named Student. Java tells them apart by their parameter lists.
name = studentName; copies the parameter into the field.
new Student("Maya", 10, 3.8) must list the arguments in the same order and types as the parameters.
pitfall: If you write only the parameterized constructor, Java no longer gives you a default one, so new Student() causes the compile error: constructor Student in class Student cannot be applied to given types.
